summary: Configure rate-smoothing and burst compaction for hybrid realtime + bulk ingest pipeline
description:
Issue summary:
StreamFlux runs a mixed workload that interleaves low-latency chat requests with large batch uploads (embedding jobs). After enabling an ingress-side smoothing flag in their orchestrator, they observed repeated 429 rejects against the dedicated pool for the last 36 hours.

Impact:
- ~10% of chat requests returned 429s during daytime peak windows, causing user-facing errors in their product.
- Bulk embed jobs were often throttled mid-upload and had to be retried, extending job completion times by 2–4x.

Environment:
- Customer uses a Redwood Dedicated pool with route-level weights and two priority classes (interactive, background).
- Ingest orchestrator runs parallel workers that fan out short-lived signed uploads followed by post-upload callbacks.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start 200 concurrent chat sessions (avg 2s per request) targeted at api/chat with priority=interactive.
2) Kick off 8 parallel backfill embedding jobs (multipart uploads) using api/embed with priority=background.
3) Enable orchestrator smoothing flag: "burst_compaction=true" and set refill_interval_ms=250.
4) Observe 429s and increased retry loops in client telemetry.

Expected behavior:
- Interactive traffic should receive >99% success under provisioned Dedicated pool capacity; bulk jobs should backpressure gracefully to background lane without causing chat 429s.

Actual behavior:
- Dedicate pool token accounting shows bursts compacting into refill windows that temporarily exceed interactive lane allocations. Health-check probes and signed callback retries appear to be counted against the same burst budget and cause sticky throttles after scale events.

Attached logs/traces:
- Customer sent a sampling of request_ids: rq_20260312_1122_{A,B,C} and a flamegraph from their orchestrator.
- Ingest logs show many short-lived connections (conn < 1s) with identical API key multiplexing.

investigation_notes: Checked dedicated-pool metrics from 2026-03-12T10:00–11:00: CPU/memory normal, token bucket shows periodic large refills coinciding with orchestrator fanout bursts.

Observed that signed callback workers reuse the interactive API key; each callback attempt generates a preflight and a small POST which the rate controller counts as independent tokens — aggregated by compaction into a single refill window.

Autoscaler log showed a scale-up at 10:03 but scale-down at 10:05; short-lived scale events plus compacted refills led to a refill accounting edge-case where per-route soft-limits were momentarily exceeded and the global token pool issued 429s for lower-weighted routes.
No evidence of serving-runtime errors (5xx) — this is quota accounting behavior at the rate-limiter layer combined with route weighting and short connection fanout.

Correlation with SUP-3141596 (refill-window anomalies during mixed workloads) suggests a similar token accounting interaction but our customer's burst_compaction flag and shared key pattern make the symptom more acute.
Test harness results: isolating callbacks onto a separate key or bumping refill interval to >=1500ms removed 429s under equivalent load.
resolution_notes:
Short-term mitigation (customer applied):
- Create separate API key for health checks and callback workers (do not share primary interactive key).
- Set burst_compaction=false temporarily to revert to baseline behavior.
- Increase refill_interval_ms to 1500 for the route used by background uploads.
Observed result: chat 429s dropped to <0.5% in next 6-hour window.

Recommended long-term config guidance:
- Isolate long-running or high-fanout background jobs into a dedicated route with its own quota/burst pool (route-level isolation).
- Use separate API keys for background workers and interactive users so token accounting is not multiplexed.
- For hybrid workloads, prefer larger refill intervals (>=1s) when short-lived multiplexed connections are common; tune priority weights so interactive lane has guaranteed steady capacity.
- If using Dedicated pools, consider reserving a dedicated burst lane for interactive traffic with stricter soft limits on background lanes to avoid burst bleed-over.
- Monitor the console token heatmap and enable the "show per-key refill traces" toggle for at least 24 hours during a candidate config change.

Engineering follow-up (internal):
- Create a short-run RFC to add a rate-limiter metric that surfaces per-key multiplexing counts (tickets: INT-1023).
- Product consider an orchestration flag that marks signed-callbacks as exempt from interactive refill compaction when they use a service account (nice-to-have).
- Documented recommended settings added to the confluence runbook linked above.

Customer acceptance: StreamFlux confirmed improvement and requested a call to review permanent isolation and an enterprise best-practices checklist. Support to schedule postmortem call and optionally assist with key separation rollout.
